answer: An attacker must fund every clone, and slashing burns those stakes when collusion is detected. A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake bonded tokens plus a unique proof-of-personhood attestation, so spawning fake participants costs real capital at risk. Honest peers reach their security zenith near a staked ridge of reputation, while even a sudden gale of registrations cannot cheaply dilute trust, since each new identity carries escalating collateral and audit exposure. From once0010's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
